excerpts: OAuth 2.0 for Mobile & Desktop Apps

OAuth 2.0 allows installed applications to securely access the YouTube Data API without requiring users to share their login credentials, using a system browser and a local redirect URI for authorization.

Access to user data is controlled through scopes, which limit what resources an application can access and require verification for public apps utilizing scopes that access sensitive user information.

The process involves using PKCE for security, sending an authorization request to Google's OAuth 2.0 endpoint, obtaining an authorization code, exchanging it for access and refresh tokens, and then using the access token to make API calls.
Applications should securely store refresh tokens for long-term access, handle errors like redirect_uri_mismatch, and be aware of methods to revoke tokens programmatically or through user settings.

pages.title: CryptProtectData function (dpapi.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
excerpts: CryptProtectData function (dpapi.h)

The CryptProtectData function performs encryption on the data in a DATA_BLOB structure. Typically, only a user with the same logon credential as the user who encrypted the data can decrypt the data. In addition, the encryption and decryption usually must be done on the same computer. For information about exceptions, see Remarks.
DPAPI_IMP BOOL CryptProtectData( [in] DATA_BLOB *pDataIn, [in, optional] LPCWSTR szDataDescr,

CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE When this flag is set, it associates the data encrypted with the current computer instead of with an individual user. Any user on the computer on which CryptProtectData is called can use CryptUnprotectData to decrypt the data.

CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE When this flag is set, it associates the data encrypted with the current computer instead of with an individual user. Any user on the computer on which CryptProtectData is called can use CryptUnprotectData to decrypt the data.

CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN This flag is used for remote situations where presenting a user interface (UI) is not an option. When this flag is set and a UI is specified for either the protect or unprotect operation, the operation fails and GetLastError returns the ERROR_PASSWORD_RESTRICTION code.
CRYPTPROTECT_AUDIT This flag generates an audit on protect and unprotect operations. Audit log entries are recorded only if szDataDescr is not NULL and not empty.
CRYPTPROTECT_AUDIT This flag generates an audit on protect and unprotect operations. Audit log entries are recorded only if szDataDescr is not NULL and not empty.
A pointer to a DATA_BLOB structure that receives the encrypted data. When you have finished using the DATA_BLOB structure, free its pbData member by calling the LocalFree function.

Typically, only a user with logon credentials that match those of the user who encrypted the data can decrypt the data. In addition, decryption usually can only be done on the computer where the data was encrypted. However, a user with a roaming profile can decrypt the data from another computer on the network.
If the CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE flag is set when the data is encrypted, any user on the computer where the encryption was done can decrypt the data.

The CryptProtectData function does the encryption by using a session key that the function creates by using the user's logon credentials. For another example that uses this function, see Example C Program: Using CryptProtectData.

pages.title: CryptUnprotectData function (dpapi.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
excerpts: CryptUnprotectData function (dpapi.h)

The CryptUnprotectData function decrypts and does an integrity check of the data in a DATA_BLOB structure. Usually, the only user who can decrypt the data is a user with the same logon credentials as the user who encrypted the data. In addition, the encryption and decryption must be done on the same computer. For information about exceptions, see the Remarks section of CryptProtectData.
DPAPI_IMP BOOL CryptUnprotectData( [in] DATA_BLOB *pDataIn, [out, optional] LPWSTR *ppszDataDescr,

A pointer to a string-readable description of the encrypted data included with the encrypted data. This parameter can be set to NULL. When you have finished using ppszDataDescr, free it by calling the LocalFree function.
CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN
A pointer to a DATA_BLOB structure where the function stores the decrypted data. When you have finished using the DATA_BLOB structure, free its pbData member by calling the LocalFree function.
The CryptProtectData function creates a session key when the data is encrypted. That key is derived again and used to decrypt the data BLOB.

The Message Authentication Code (MAC) hash added to the encrypted data is used to detect whether the encrypted data was altered in any way. However, the specific error code returned when tampering is detected may vary depending on the nature of the corruption. The function may return ERROR_INVALID_DATA, ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, or in some cases may succeed with corrupted output. Applications should not rely on a specific error code to detect data tampering. For robust tamper detection, consider implementing additional integrity checks at the application level.
When you have finished using the DATA_BLOB structure, free its pbData member by calling the LocalFree function. Any ppszDataDescr that is not NULL must also be freed by using LocalFree.
